name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}-6y=18\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),\,y(0)=2
$$

Given that the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{′}-6y=18\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}=A{e}^{6x},$ solve the initial value problem.

worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
{y}_{c}^{′}-6{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{6x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $18\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}=-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-6(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))=18\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(-6\alpha +3\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+(-3\alpha -6\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)=18\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6\alpha +3\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of }\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)) \\ -3\alpha -6\beta =18\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of }\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{6}{5},\text{ }\beta =-\frac{12}{5}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{6}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{12}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{6x}-\frac{6}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{12}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Now, we can find the constant $A$ using the initial conditions.

Substituting $y(0)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A{e}^{6\cdot 0}-\frac{6}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)-\frac{12}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0) & =2 \\ A-\frac{6}{5}-0 & =2 \\ A & =\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=\frac{16}{5}{e}^{6x}-\frac{6}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{12}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$
